title: Inline and Reified Generic Functions
learning_outcomes: Explain the central rule or purpose of inline and reified generic functions using at least one correct term from the lesson.

Identify one relevant edge case, debugging step, or version/platform constraint.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn **Inline and Reified Generic Functions** as part of **Generics and Type-System Design**. Kotlin functions can expose parameters and return types, and function values/lambdas allow behavior to be passed to or returned from other functions. Use the subtopics—The inline Modifier, reified Type Parameters, Binary Compatibility Considerations—as a checklist: predict what the example will do, then verify it in a project configured for the target platform.
content.why_it_matters: These concepts help you model domain rules and reusable APIs. Good boundaries reduce accidental mutation, unsafe casts, and code that is difficult to extend.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Kotlin functions can expose parameters and return types, and function values/lambdas allow behavior to be passed to or returned from other functions.

content_blocks.title: How to reason about it
content_blocks.text: Start with the inline modifier. Then compare it with reified type parameters. Identify the input, state, dependency, or branch that determines the result. The snippet is a static reference for CodeLeaf and is not executed in the lesson page.

items.title: The inline Modifier
items.text: The inline Modifier is one part of inline and reified generic functions. Connect its definition to the example, identify the input/state it changes, and verify the expected behavior with a small test case.

items.title: reified Type Parameters
items.text: reified Type Parameters describes how behavior is declared, passed, or composed. Make inputs and return types clear, keep side effects visible, and use a small call-site example to judge readability.

items.title: Binary Compatibility Considerations
items.text: Binary Compatibility Considerations means checking the boundary between the language feature and its compiler, runtime, plugin, library, or target version. Pin the versions used by the project and verify documented support before depending on the behavior.
